terms.comment: The adjective of septentriōnēs, the seven stars of the Plough and so the north (see north). Cicero and Caesar more often use the noun with a preposition, ad septentriōnēs; as a noun, septentriōnālia are the northern parts.

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.50: quae tum est aquilōnia tum austrālis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From aquilō, the north wind (see north wind).

phrases.latin: quae tum est aquilōnia tum austrālis
phrases.english: which is now northern, now southern

sources: Lewis & Short: septentrionalis · Lewis & Short: septentriones · Lewis & Short: aquilonius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 205, 352.
Varro, Pliny, Tacitus and Cicero as Lewis & Short cites them.
